mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 5-year rolling windows is less than 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 10% within a 3-month window signals a severe labor market contraction, prompting central bank intervention and fiscal stimulus that boost equity returns over the subsequent 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 10% for at least one month, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 in any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based demand contraction, which triggers a policy response that subsequently lifts equity markets; the interaction effect is stronger than either series alone.
failure_condition: The interaction effect (joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS) fails to predict positive returns in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.02 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a manufacturing slowdown (INDPRO below 95 for two consecutive months), the Federal Reserve typically implements accommodative policies that support equity markets, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO is below 95 for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly expansion in real GDP (GDPC1) above the 1.5% annualized growth rate indicates a strengthening economy, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 growth exceeds 1.5% annualized, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the core inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) above 3.0% for two consecutive months signals an inflationary environment that may lead to tighter monetary policy, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL inflation exceeds 3.0% for two months, or the Rank IC is below -0.02 in any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment (PAYEMS) and rise in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a deteriorating labor market, which often precedes economic stimulus and leads to positive equity returns over the next 20 trading days; the joint effect is stronger than either series alone.
failure_condition: The joint signal (decline in PAYEMS and rise in UNRATE) fails to predict positive returns in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.02 in any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During a period of active Federal Reserve rate cuts (FEDFUNDS falling below 0.5% in the last 3 months), the resulting liquidity injection and risk-on sentiment drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS has fallen below 0.5% in the last 3 months, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over any 3-year window.
